score.note: First structural draft, not a permutation search. Reached this score after three evidence-guided respellings: (1) reading the two consecutive globals at 0x03001EEC/0x03001EF0 (work pointer, secondary draw-destination pointer) as two independent raw-address dereferences rather than a shared struct -- a struct-typed read was tried first (hoping to reproduce the reference's ldmia r3!,{r1} prologue idiom) but it compiled to two ordinary ldr instructions anyway and regressed the score (281->317 differing halfwords), so the plain dereference form was kept; (2) caching the address of work's 0x7828 field (a void** slot) in one local computed once before the per-member do/while loop, instead of recomputing M2C_FIELD(work,...,0x7828) from scratch at every use -- this matches the reference's own 'adds r7,r1,r2' (compute address once) followed by repeated 'ldr r3,[r7,#0]' (dereference only) and improved 280->286 differing halfwords is misleading in isolation, see next point; (3) fixing a genuine rounding-toward-zero halving bug in the bounce-damping expression (was `(bounced + (u32)bounced >> 31) >> 1` due to C operator precedence putting the outer >>1 over only the >>31 term instead of over the whole sum; corrected to `(bounced + ((u32)bounced >> 31)) >> 1` to match the reference's negs/lsrs/adds/asrs sequence) -- this is a real semantic correction kept even though it nudged the raw score slightly worse (280/295/660 -> 286/298/668), because reproducing the reference's actual rounding behavior matters more than a coincidental byte-count improvement from a wrong formula.

This owner and its three siblings (080d82b0, 080dc1ec, 080e01e4, also assigned to me) plus 080e7404 all appear to be members of one 'battle presentation sub-effect' family keyed off that same 0x03001eec work block, not the orbiting_particles family. rejected_experiments: Struct-typed single read of the two leading 0x03001EEC/0x03001EF0 globals (hoping to reproduce the reference's ldmia r3!,{r1} load-multiple prologue): compiled to two ordinary back-to-back ldr instructions instead of ldmia and regressed differing_halfwords from 281 to 317; reverted to two independent raw-pointer dereferences.

Hoisting the two function-pointer reads at 0x03001F08/0x03001F0C (draw_rectangle/alt_draw_rectangle) into named locals read once right after the two Func_080ed408 calls, matching the reference's own early read+stack-spill of these values: this is structurally what the reference does (str to sp+12/sp+16, later reload), but declaring them as ordinary C locals kept them live across the entire 148-frame outer loop in this compiler's allocator and regressed the score (281->309); reverted to inline point-of-use dereferences of the fixed addresses, which the compiler happened to schedule closer to the reference's own load sites.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect. Seeds a 32-entry sprite-record pool at 0x02010000 with randomized initial falling parameters, opens two display windows (ids 46 and 47), then runs 148 frames. Each frame conditionally walks the active work-target's member list (drawing/positioning each member's portrait via Func_08004cb4 and occasionally cueing Func_080d6888), then integrates simple bounce physics (gravity accumulator, velocity, halved rebound damping) over the first 12 sprite records and draws each active one through one of two rectangle-callback function pointers selected by a phase-derived 0-7 'kind' value, alternating draw target by whether kind is 0-3 or 4-7.

The 'unemittable' class and the 286/298 residual mean the source shape is still meaningfully off from the reference in several places this pass did not fully resolve: notably the reference keeps the shared work pointer in r9 for the whole function while this compiler consistently chooses fp/r11 for it, and Func_080072f4's calling convention (observed passing a 5th argument through r4, beyond r0-r3, before two more stack-passed arguments) is not fully understood -- both are recorded here as concrete, evidence-backed open questions rather than guessed away.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
